rationale: PINS the K6 gap: an anonymous object (object : Runner { ... }) is a real runtime type. It must (1) get a symbol named after its implemented supertype (anonymous_Runner — the established anonymous_* noise convention, so it never leaks into the index), (2) own its contained members (go() attributes to the anonymous object, NOT the enclosing class P — the previous P->go contains edge was a misattribution), and (3) reference its implemented type (run -> Runner). UPDATED by the M49/M37 #867 ruling: this fixture's literal sits inside `fun run()`, and it used to pin the anon type's OWN owner as the enclosing class `P` — the one place in the suite where kotlin's outlier behaviour was enshrined. Under the ruling (ownerName = the innermost enclosing DECLARATION, matching java/groovy/scala) the owner is the method `run`; kotlin was the analyzer that changed. The other pin here — that `go()` is owned by the anonymous object rather than by `P` — is unchanged and unrelated.
